newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission resists changes to veal premium.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission resists changes to veal premium.

text.p: The European Commission will resist calls for changes to the veal early marketing premium at Tuesday's meeting of European Union farm ministers, an official said on Friday.
France has asked for the scheme, aimed at reducing beef production, to be suspended because it says is undermining its veal market, the official explained.
"The French and the British say the scheme distorts the market but the Commission feels it is too early to draw conclusions, the official said.
Britain, whose officials expect 60 percent of all young veal calves slaughtered under the scheme this year to be in the United Kingdom, has not asked for the scheme to be suspended.
Last month a Commission report on the scheme said that although the early marketing scheme had done little to cut red meat production it should be judged over a longer period.
It added that the so-called Herod scheme, which subsidises the slaughter of animals up to 10 months old, had proved to be very efficient and cost effective.
France has campaigned for an end to the scheme because it says it favours Dutch farmers to export veal to France.
But, the report said, there was no statistical evidence to support the French claim, adding that prices in the Netherlands were traditionally lower than in France. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
